  PROBLEM: The `workflow_run.workflows` filter `["*"]` may not match arbitrary workflow names, preventing the consumer triage wrapper from being dispatched for their workflow runs.
  WHY: If GitHub treats `*` as a literal workflow name, consumer failures will not be triaged; other reviewers dispute this finding, stating that GitHub supports `*` as a wildcard.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "**Trigger:** a failed (`failure` or `timed_out`) pull-request run of a GitHub Actions workflow, through `workflow_run: completed` (job `triage-workflow-run`) ... This repo's wrapper listens to the `CI` workflow; the consumer wrapper listens to every workflow (`"*"`) and skips the pipeline's own `AI …` workflows, so each finished workflow also leaves a skipped wrapper run in the Actions tab." (PR description, "Which workflows (Q55)")
  expected_change_site: tests/test_ci_failure_workflow_run_triggers.py:111-119 (test_consumer_wrapper_listens_to_every_workflow_but_its_own) and the consumer wrapper at workflow-templates/ai-check-failure-triage.yml:14-18.
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The shipped test asserts the configured string `workflows: ["*"]` and exercises the job-level `if:` condition with synthetic events, but never asserts that GitHub's `workflow_run` dispatcher actually delivers the wrapper for a non-AI, non-CI workflow name. The README claim "each finished workflow ... leaves a skipped wrapper run in the Actions tab" is not pinned by any contract test against the rendered workflow file or GitHub's documented behavior.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
